_meta.purpose: Initial RSI Hermes ship + zone definitions.
_meta.axis_convention: Width = port-to-starboard (X). Length = rear-ramp-edge to forward (Y). Height = floor up (Z). All units are 1.25 m cubes.
_meta.ramp_note: Single rear ramp. All bays load via low-Y (rear) end. Ship-forward direction is high-Y.
_meta.load_doctrine_note: Eight bays in four side-by-side columns. Each column has a Rear bay (R) at low-Y and a Forward bay (F) behind it at high-Y, so to access F the loader walks past R first. Loading direction = walk forward, deepest first: F1-F4 are loaded FIRST (and unload LAST), R1-R4 are loaded LAST (and unload FIRST). unload_priority encodes this: R1..R4 = 1..4 (drained first), F1..F4 = 5..8 (drained last). The planner naturally places early-delivery cargo in R bays and final/return cargo deep in F bays.
_meta.f_r_continuity_note: Within a column, F and R bays are physically continuous (no bulkhead). The schema's left/right adjacency captures horizontal neighbors only; the F-to-R join is implicit in shared cube_offset_x.
_meta.column_break_note: There is a physical break between columns 2 and 3 (between F2/R2 and F3/R3). Currently modeled as zero-width gap (cube_offset_x jumps from 2..4 with no zone in between). If the break turns out to be loadable as a bulk slot, add it as a new zone with unload_priority = 9 (absolute last resort).
_meta.side_pad_note: Per the Hermes cargo grid diagram the ship has TWO additional 16-SCU pads (yellow) beyond the eight 32-SCU bays, taking the catalog total to 288 SCU. Their exact placement is TBD — likely standalone elevator pads at the rear ramp. Not modeled here; modeled capacity is 256 SCU until confirmed. ship.total_scu is set to the catalog 288 so the ships table matches the manufacturer spec; the planner uses the sum of ship_zones rows (256) as actual capacity.
_meta.scu_rating_note: Each main bay is 2x9x2 = 36 cube units physically but rated 32 SCU practical (one row of cubes is lost to pallet/pad alignment, matching the in-game 4x8-SCU pads-per-bay layout). scu_capacity = 32 reflects what reliably loads.

zones.notes: Forward bay, port column. Loaded FIRST (deepest) so cargo here unloads LAST — best place for return/final-destination cargo. 2x9x2 cube footprint, 32 SCU rated.
Forward bay, mid-starboard column. Note: physical break separates F2/F3 columns from F3/F4.
Rear bay, port column. Loaded LAST (nearest ramp) so cargo here unloads FIRST — best place for early-delivery cargo.
